about: Ascension: each class chooses 1 of 2 ascendancies (like Path of Exile 2). You get 1 Ascension point for each area finale boss you beat (5 in total). Each board has 8 nodes: tier 1 is open from the start, tier 2 opens at tierCosts[1] points spent, and tier 3 (the capstones) at tierCosts[2]; you can only take one capstone. stats work like the skill tree's (damage, hp, time, heal, weakness, dodge, defense, xp), plus the special ones listed in js/ascension.js. Resetting is free.

ascendancies.name: Blue Team Lead
ascendancies.description: Leads the defenders: blocks the first blow, caps big hits, and strikes back when attacks miss.

nodes.name: Hardened Perimeter
nodes.text: +40 max health
nodes.concept: Perimeter security: the controls at the edge of a network, like firewalls and gateways.

nodes.name: Preventive Control
nodes.text: The first enemy hit in each fight is fully blocked
nodes.concept: Preventive control: a control that stops an incident before it happens.

nodes.name: Rate Limiting
nodes.text: No single hit can take more than 25% of your max health
nodes.concept: Rate limiting: capping how many requests get through, so one source can't overwhelm a system.

nodes.name: Countermeasure
nodes.text: When an enemy misses you, strike back for 30% of your last hit
nodes.concept: Countermeasure: an action or control that answers a threat.

nodes.name: Fail-Safe
nodes.text: Once per fight, a killing blow leaves you at 1 health (works on top of Failover Core)
nodes.concept: Fail-safe design: when something breaks, it ends up in a safe state.

nodes.name: Continuous Monitoring
nodes.text: Enemies hit 8% less often
nodes.concept: Continuous monitoring: watching systems all the time, so problems are caught early.

nodes.name: Incident Commander
nodes.text: Every 3 right answers in a row heal 20% of your max health
nodes.concept: Incident commander: the person who leads the response team during an incident.

nodes.name: Compensating Control
nodes.text: Take 25% less damage while below half health
nodes.concept: Compensating control: a backup control used when the main one can't do the job.

ascendancies.name: Firewall Architect
ascendancies.description: Designs the walls: rules, zones and filters. Enemies that hit you get hurt too.

nodes.name: Implicit Deny
nodes.text: Enemies hit 6% less often
nodes.concept: Implicit deny: anything a rule doesn't explicitly allow is blocked.

nodes.name: Port Security
nodes.text: +30 max health
nodes.concept: Port security: limiting which devices can use a switch port, often by MAC address.

nodes.name: Packet Filtering
nodes.text: Take 10% less damage
nodes.concept: Packet filtering: allowing or blocking traffic by address, port and protocol.

nodes.name: Stateful Inspection
nodes.text: When an enemy hits you, it takes 50% of that damage back
nodes.concept: Stateful inspection: a firewall that tracks connections, so only replies to traffic you started get back in.

nodes.name: Access Control List
nodes.text: +10% skill damage
nodes.concept: ACL: an ordered list of rules saying which traffic or users are allowed or denied.

nodes.name: Ingress Filtering
nodes.text: Bosses deal 15% less damage to you
nodes.concept: Ingress filtering: checking traffic coming into a network and dropping what doesn't belong.

nodes.name: Next-Gen Firewall
nodes.text: Every time an enemy misses you, heal 8% of your max health
nodes.concept: Next-generation firewall (NGFW): a firewall that understands applications and can block attacks hidden in allowed traffic.

nodes.name: Air Gap
nodes.text: The first 2 enemy hits in each fight are blocked, but you have 15% less max health
nodes.concept: Air gap: a system with no network connection to anything else.

ascendancies.name: Threat Hunter
ascendancies.description: Goes looking for attackers before the alarms go off. Rewards answer streaks and weak points.

nodes.name: Triage
nodes.text: Heal 4 more health per right answer
nodes.concept: Triage: sorting alerts and incidents so the most serious get handled first.

nodes.name: Behavioral Analysis
nodes.text: Weak points take +0.25x more damage
nodes.concept: Behavioral analysis: spotting attacks by unusual behavior instead of known signatures.

nodes.name: Correlation
nodes.text: After a right answer, the enemy's attack is 15% less likely to hit
nodes.concept: Correlation: linking events from different logs to see one bigger attack (a SIEM does this).

nodes.name: Threat Feed
nodes.text: Each right answer in a row adds +8% damage (up to +40%). A miss resets it.
nodes.concept: Threat feed: a steady stream of fresh threat data that keeps improving your detections.

nodes.name: Root Cause Analysis
nodes.text: Bosses take +20% damage
nodes.concept: Root cause analysis: finding the real reason an incident happened, so it doesn't happen again.

nodes.name: Lessons Learned
nodes.text: A wrong answer heals you for 5 (you still learn from it)
nodes.concept: Lessons learned: the review after an incident, to do better next time.

nodes.name: Full Visibility
nodes.text: Hitting a weak point also heals 10% of your max health
nodes.concept: Visibility: you can't defend what you can't see. Logs and monitoring give you the view.

nodes.name: SOAR Playbook
nodes.text: Wrong answers and timeouts still deal 35% of the skill's damage
nodes.concept: SOAR (security orchestration, automation and response): playbooks that act even when people are busy.

ascendancies.name: Forensic Investigator
ascendancies.description: Collects the evidence and rebuilds what really happened. More time, and help ruling out wrong answers.

nodes.name: Chain of Custody
nodes.text: +6 seconds per question
nodes.concept: Chain of custody: a record of everyone who handled evidence, so it holds up in court.

nodes.name: Legal Hold
nodes.text: +25 max health
nodes.concept: Legal hold: an order to keep data that might be needed in a lawsuit.

nodes.name: Timeline
nodes.text: +10% skill damage
nodes.concept: Timeline: putting events in order to see how an attack unfolded.

nodes.name: Write Blocker
nodes.text: After a wrong answer, the enemy's attack that turn deals 15% less
nodes.concept: Write blocker: a device that lets you read a drive without changing anything on it.

nodes.name: Order of Volatility
nodes.text: Your first hit in each fight deals +40%
nodes.concept: Order of volatility: collect the evidence that disappears fastest (like RAM) first.

nodes.name: E-Discovery
nodes.concept: E-discovery: finding and handing over electronic records for a legal case.

nodes.name: Expert Witness
nodes.text: One wrong answer is crossed out on every question
nodes.concept: Expert witness: a specialist who explains technical evidence to a court.

nodes.name: Disk Image
nodes.text: Once per fight, when you drop below 30% health, heal back to 60%
nodes.concept: Disk image: an exact bit-for-bit copy of a drive, so analysis never touches the original.

ascendancies.name: Cipher Master
ascendancies.description: Bends cryptography into raw damage: critical hits, big openers and boss slaying.

nodes.name: Key Stretching
nodes.text: +12% skill damage
nodes.concept: Key stretching: hashing a password many times so it's slow to crack (PBKDF2, bcrypt).

nodes.name: Salting
nodes.text: 15% chance for a critical hit (double damage)
nodes.concept: Salting: adding random data to each password before hashing, so identical passwords get different hashes.

nodes.name: Key Rotation
nodes.text: +25 max health
nodes.concept: Key rotation: replacing keys on a schedule, so a stolen key is useful for less time.

nodes.name: Forward Secrecy
nodes.text: Your first hit in each fight deals +75%
nodes.concept: Perfect forward secrecy: each session gets its own key, so one stolen key can't unlock past sessions.

nodes.name: Post-Quantum
nodes.text: Bosses take +20% damage
nodes.concept: Post-quantum cryptography: algorithms designed to stay safe even against quantum computers.

nodes.name: Entropy
nodes.text: Critical hits deal 2.5x instead of 2x
nodes.concept: Entropy: true randomness. Keys need lots of it to be hard to guess.

nodes.name: One-Time Pad
nodes.text: Every 4th right answer in a fight is an automatic critical hit
nodes.concept: One-time pad: a random key as long as the message, used once. Unbreakable if done right.

nodes.name: Elliptic Curve
nodes.text: +30% skill damage, but enemies hit 5% more often
nodes.concept: Elliptic curve cryptography (ECC): strong encryption with small keys, good for phones and small devices.

ascendancies.name: PKI Warden
ascendancies.description: Guards the chain of trust: certificates, keys and signatures. Tougher, and heals from its own hits.

nodes.name: Root of Trust
nodes.text: +30 max health
nodes.concept: Root of trust: the starting point everything else trusts, like a root CA or a TPM chip.

nodes.name: Certificate Pinning
nodes.text: Enemies hit 5% less often
nodes.concept: Certificate pinning: an app only accepts one specific certificate, which blocks fake ones.

nodes.name: Digital Signature
nodes.text: +10% skill damage
nodes.concept: Digital signature: a hash signed with the sender's private key. Proves who sent it and that it wasn't changed.

nodes.name: Key Escrow
nodes.text: Once per fight, a killing blow leaves you at 1 health (works on top of Failover Core)
nodes.concept: Key escrow: a trusted third party keeps a copy of a key so it can be recovered.

nodes.name: Revocation
nodes.text: Each of your hits makes the enemy 2% less likely to hit you this fight (up to 10%)
nodes.concept: Certificate revocation: cancelling a certificate before it expires, checked with a CRL or OCSP.

nodes.name: OCSP Stapling
nodes.text: Heal 4 health per right answer
nodes.concept: OCSP stapling: the server attaches a fresh "still valid" proof to its certificate, so clients don't have to ask.

nodes.name: Certificate Authority
nodes.text: Heal for 10% of the damage you deal
nodes.concept: Certificate authority (CA): the trusted organization that issues and signs certificates.

nodes.name: Wildcard Certificate
nodes.text: 25% chance that any hit counts as a weak-point hit
nodes.concept: Wildcard certificate: one certificate that covers every subdomain, like *.example.com.
